title: Module 8 Vocabulary Check
intro: Answer each item. Feedback comes right away. Items you miss come back for a retry round.

o: Separate groups of participants in each condition
The same participants in each condition
items.why: Different people provide the scores in each condition, so the scores are independent.

items.q: The null hypothesis for an independent-measures t test is typically
items.why: It says the two populations have the same mean.

items.q: Degrees of freedom for the independent-measures t are
items.why: Each group contributes n minus 1 degrees of freedom, so the total is n1 plus n2 minus 2.

o: A weighted average of the two sample variances
The sum of the two means
The larger of the two variances
items.why: It combines information from both samples into one estimate of the common population variance.

o: The two populations have equal variances
The two samples have equal means
items.why: Pooling is justified only when the variances are similar.

items.q: The standard error of the difference between means
o: Estimates how far a difference between two sample means typically falls from the true difference
Equals the SD of the scores
Is always smaller than either sample SE
items.why: It is the denominator of the independent-measures t.

items.q: If the two groups have unequal sample sizes and very different variances, a good practice is to
o: Use a version of the test that does not assume equal variances
items.why: Welch's test adjusts the degrees of freedom and does not pool variances.

items.q: Cohen's d for two independent groups divides the mean difference by
o: The standard error of the difference
items.why: The pooled SD puts the difference in standard deviation units, independent of sample size.

items.q: A larger difference between sample means, with all else equal, will
items.why: The mean difference is the numerator of t.

items.q: Random assignment of participants to two groups helps ensure that
o: The groups are comparable before treatment, supporting causal inference
The samples are representative of the population
items.why: It controls for pre-existing differences on average, which is what gives the design its causal leverage.
